 Former PBA star PJ Simon passes away
 Rom Anzures ,
 ABS-CBN News
 Published November 21, 2026 12:38 AM PHT 
 Former Magnolia Hotshots star Peter June Simon. PBA Images. MANILA — PJ Simon, an eight-time PBA champion, has passed away.
 He was 46.
 His former team, the Magnolia Hotshots, confirmed the sad news on social media.
 “We will remember every moment, because you made each one unforgettable,” the Hotshots wrote in their post. “To PJ’s family and loved ones, we’re holding you close in our hearts. Maraming salamat sa lahat, PJ.”
 ADVERTISEMENT
 The 16-year PBA veteran was seen having difficulty breathing on the bench during a game in Davao before being carried by players to an ambulance, as shown in videos circulating online.
 The “Scoring Apostle” spent his entire PBA career with the Purefoods/Magnolia franchise, which retired his No. 8 jersey in 2021, a year after his retirement.
 He was among Purefoods' most beloved players alongside James Yap and Marc Pingris, with the trio leading the then-San Mig Super Coffee Mixers to a historic PBA Grand Slam in the 2013-14 season.
 The Cotabato-born guard was selected by Sta. Lucia as the 43rd overall pick in the fifth round of the 2001 PBA Draft but went unsigned before eventually suiting up for Purefoods three years later.
 Simon's last PBA title came in the 2018 Governors' Cup, when Purefoods defeated the Alaska Aces. It was also the franchise's most recent PBA championship.
